prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Protactinium (프로트악티늄) itself — the sovereign of the Protactinium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: late thirties — a glamorous, alluring mature beauty in her prime: confident, sensual poise, a knowing gaze and a ripe, womanly figure; smooth, radiant skin with at most the faintest lines at the eye corners; never old, tired, gaunt or matronly — still the small, soft chin and soft contours.
Face — her own: a mature, poised woman; bronze-brown skin; round face; medium-sized eyes — long monolid eyes, outer eye corners drooping downward; low heavy brows; broad soft nose; soft medium lips; silver-grey eyes; a small beauty mark beside the lips.
Body and hair: pear-shaped and curvaceous — slimmer shoulders over a narrow waist, full rounded hips and thick thighs, a full bust build; an updo bun with center-parted bangs framing the face; lustrous silver-grey hair with a pitch-black underlayer, like a vein of metal in dark ore.
Expression: a warm, gentle look with a faint smile.
Her element, carried in her design: protactinium: a dense, bright silvery metal hidden in uranium ore at well under a gram per tonne, named the mother of actinium because it decays into actinium; first glimpsed in 1913 as a form lasting about a minute and called brevium, the short one, then found in 1918 in Berlin in a form that lives tens of thousands of years by a pair of researchers, one of whom had begun her work in a converted carpentry workshop; among the rarest and costliest elements, the world's supply for decades was about 125 grams painstakingly recovered from 60 tonnes of uranium waste; its ratio to thorium in deep-sea mud records the paths of ancient ocean currents.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. Bright silvery armor with several rigid jointed plates flaring from the waist like a skirt, plates not cloth, each lower plate shaped like a small open launch bay marked with a tiny ship emblem and the legs showing between them, a pitch-black inner suit with deep-sea teal seams, a cradle-shaped core at the chest; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: several rigid jointed armor plates flaring from the waist like a skirt — plates, not cloth — with the legs showing between them. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: bright silvery metal, pitchblende black, deep-sea mud teal, warm cradle-wood honey.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, a mothership city that gives birth to ships: a vast bright silver mothership ringed with dark ore holds, launching daughter ships from its open bays, each daughter in turn sending out a smaller granddaughter craft across the sky, and a deep-sea deck where long cores of seabed mud are drawn up to read the currents of ancient oceans.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Pa) and atomic number (91) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
